meta.origin: Ashkenazi Jewish folk dance music, Eastern Europe (Moldova, Ukraine, Romania)
meta.typical_form: AABB (binary dance form), often with coda (a freylekhs tants)
meta.mood: Joyful, celebratory, driving dance with melancholic modal inflections

pitch.name: Freygish (Phrygian Dominant) Scale
pitch.description: G Freygish: G (root), Ab (minor 2nd), B (major 3rd), C (perfect 4th), D (perfect 5th), Eb (minor 6th), F (minor 7th), G (octave). The augmented 2nd between Ab and B creates the signature 'Jewish' interval. Melodies often emphasize the flat 2nd (Ab) resolving to the root, and the major 3rd (B) as a leading tone to the 4th (C).

characteristic_motifs.name: Tsimbl riff
characteristic_motifs.description: Descending cadential figure landing on tonic

characteristic_motifs.name: Dreydlekh (turn)
characteristic_motifs.description: Ornamental turn around the tonic area

rhythm.name: Freylekhs Dance Rhythm (2/4)

variants.name: Bass oom-pah
variants.description: Root on beat 1, fifth on beat 2 (or root octave jump)

variants.name: Secunda afterbeat
variants.description: Offbeat chordal accompaniment (secunda = 'second' in Yiddish, referring to the offbeat)

variants.name: Snare accent pattern
variants.description: Accented downbeats with offbeat snare cracks

variants.name: Terkisher (Turkish) variant
variants.description: More syncopated, influenced by Ottoman military bands

rhythm.time_feel: Driving eighth notes, slight lift on offbeats, never swung (straight eighths)

timbre.harmonic_profile: bright, nasal, with prominent upper partials (3rd–7th harmonics)

ornamentation.krechts: Portamento slide up a half-step with a quick vibrato decay — the 'cry'
ornamentation.dreydlekh: Rapid four-note turn around a principal note
ornamentation.glissando: Expressive slides between intervals, especially the augmented 2nd (Ab↔B)
ornamentation.trill: Upper neighbor trill, typically a half-step (e.g., G–Ab–G)

alternative_instruments.harmonic_profile: reedy, piercing, with strong odd harmonics (1st, 3rd, 5th)
bright, percussive attack with rapid decay, rich in inharmonic partials

unit_matrix.description: 2-bar Freylekhs pattern in 2/4 (8 eighth-note slots per row)

variations.name: Slow Hora (3/8 or 9/8)
variations.description: Slower, more lyrical dance in compound meter. Lead uses longer note values with more ornamentation.

variations.name: Doina (free improvisation)
variations.description: Rubato, improvisatory prelude. No fixed grid. Lead weeps freely over a sustained bass drone (usually tonic).

harmonic_progression.description: Gm (i) → D7 (V7) → Gm (i) → D7 (V7). The V7 chord uses F# (raised 7th of the scale) creating a strong dominant pull back to i. The flat 6 (Eb) in the scale gives the iv chord (Cm) a minor quality often used as a subdominant.

cadences.phrygian_half: iv6 → V7 (Cm/Eb → D7) — common in slower sections

structural_rules: Binary form: AABB, each section typically 8 bars
Sections contrast in register: A section lower/mid-range, B section higher/more intense
Bass oom-pah: root on downbeat, fifth on beat 2 (or octave root)
Secunda (afterbeat) is the defining klezmer rhythm marker — offbeat chordal punctuation
Lead melody uses Freygish scale with characteristic augmented 2nd (Ab↔B)
Ornamentation is structural, not decorative: krechts (cry), dreydlekh (turn), tshok (strike)
Tempo increases through the dance (accelerando toward the coda)
Final cadence often features a 'tshok' — a sharp, accented final chord with percussion hit
